title: 3SUM Breaker
one_liner: Watch why shaving an algorithm's exponent from 2.0 to 1.995 saves millions of years of compute at scale.
headline: Drag a slider to watch why a quadratic vs. n^1.995 3SUM algorithm race barely looks different — but saves millions of years once you read the numbers.

episode.title: Why Altman Says "Accept Some Bad Things Happening" and What It Means for AI Safety | MOONSHOTS #301

history.summary: A tight, mathematically honest "mission clock" demo of the 3SUM exponent result from ep. 301: the race bars, operation counts, and time-saved tally are all internally consistent (verified the math by hand), clearly labeled as simulated, and the explainer directly addresses the idea's stated risk of implying this is a reproduction of the real algorithm. The one real weakness is that the bars themselves barely diverge — which is actually the honest outcome of a ~1.0005 exponent gap — so the "race" visual underdelivers on drama relative to the big numbers doing the real work.
